fichas.title: Air-conditioning plant room arrangement
fichas.summary: Air-handling equipment must have a dedicated air-conditioning plant room in buildings of more than three storeys when connecting ductwork serves more than one storey or fire compartment. Plant rooms are commonly located on a services floor near, but not combined in the same room with, the heating and cooling plants. Their connection to vertical installation shafts and their distances from areas of demand should be considered. Services-floor placement affects the building’s appearance and requires intake and extract louvres.
fichas.building_type: Buildings with air-conditioning and ventilation systems
uses: Distribute air to multiple storeys or fire compartments

fichas.title: Sizing air-conditioning plant rooms
fichas.summary: Approximate air-conditioning plant-room area and height can be estimated from assumed volume flow and the type of air handling. The page presents charts for systems accommodating several units, with separate guidance for smaller and larger systems, and cites VDI 3803 and VDI Guideline 2052.

fichas.title: Façade ventilation systems
fichas.summary: Decentralised ventilation units are placed near façades and connected directly by ducts. Outside air is supplied directly from the façade to the unit, avoiding the need for a further air-conditioning installation in the building. Configurations include underfloor supply, combined supply and extract, and systems with central extract. Wind pressure and the façade temperature boundary layer can affect volume flow and supply-air temperature.
uses: Supply outside air near the façade
Extract air locally or through a central extract-air plant
Provide combined air supply and extract
